info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

post.description:
Syntax, role address, disposable domain and typo suggestion; a syntax
error is invalid, the rest are risky.

post.summary: Add a list's people to a campaign.
post.description:
In the background: people already members are skipped, and for an
email, social, advertising or content campaign, so are people without a
current consent for the purpose. Each member is created as `targeted`.

404.description: No such campaign or list, or the marketing package is not installed

422.description: The list holds neither contacts nor leads, or the campaign type needs a consent purpose

get.summary: Count a campaign's members by status
get.description: How many of the campaign's members are in each status.

404.description: No such campaign, or the marketing package is not installed

get.description:
Last seen, visits, purchases and their total, rolled up from the
contact's profile events when read.

404.description: No such contact, or not readable

get.description:
Sent, delivered, bounced, opened, clicked and complaints per day, sending
domain, mailbox provider and campaign, newest day first.

get.summary: Summarise DMARC reports for a domain.
get.description:
Per sending source over the window, the messages reported and how many
passed SPF and DKIM, and the sources that failed both.

200.description: SPF and DKIM per sending source

post.description:
Reads one report (XML, gzip or ZIP) and stores it, once per reporter and
report id.

requestBody.description: The report file: XML, gzip or ZIP

get.description:
Over the last `days` days: sent, delivered, bounced and complaints per
mailbox provider and day, the largest sends, the alerts raised with their
guidance keys, the latest result per target and blocklist, and each
domain's DMARC pass share, with the bounce and complaint limits in force.

Its sent, delivered, bounced, opened and clicked totals per mailbox
provider, over every day of the rollup.

parameters.name: send_id
parameters.description: The campaign the mail was sent for

200.description: The campaign's totals per mailbox provider

post.summary: Preview an email as one contact or lead.
post.description:
Resolves each dynamic block for the person (their record and lists) and
renders the design, naming the variant each block chose.

200.description: The design as the person would receive it

404.description: No such person, or the caller cannot read them

x-audit-exempt.note: renders a preview; sends and writes nothing

post.summary: Check in to a marketing event
post.description: Checks a registered person in by the code on their ticket. Audited.

200.description: Checked in (a repeat scan answers the same, not twice)

404.description: No registration for this event has that code

409.description: The registration is cancelled or still waiting

post.description: Registers a person up to the event's capacity, and puts them on the waitlist after that. Audited.

201.description: Registered, or waitlisted when the event is full

409.description: The event is closed, cancelled or done, or busy

post.description: Cancels the registration and promotes the first person waiting. Audited.

200.description: Cancelled; the first waiting person takes the seat

404.description: No such registration for this event

409.description: Already cancelled or attended, or the event is busy

post.description:
Public: a published form's submission, filed as the service account in
`marketing.form_intake.user`. Every miss (unknown, unpublished, no intake
account, marketing not licensed) is the same 404. At most five a minute
from one address and 120 a minute to one form; when the deployment has a
challenge, `captcha_token` must carry it solved (429 with
`Attome-Challenge` otherwise).

404.description: This form takes no submissions (the same answer for every reason)

422.description: No valid email, or a field is not accepted

429.description: Too many submissions, or the challenge was not solved

x-audit-exempt.note: anonymous form submission: the lead or contact, its consent events and the submission row are written by the generic create and the consent ledger, as the intake service account

get.description:
Identifiers (email, visitor, portal user, phone) a deterministic event
tied to a second contact. Nothing moved; each waits for a decision.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
One-based (D-347): page 1 is the first page. Values below 1 are
clamped up to 1 rather than rejected, matching the legacy lists.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
Rows per page, clamped to `1..=MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. Defaults to
`DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`.

post.description:
Keep the identifier with the contact it is linked to, or move it to the
conflicting contact.

get.description:
Unique visitors (website tracking page views) and conversions (form
submissions from the page) for one page path over a period of at most a
year, 30 days by default.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The landing page's path (or full URL).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start, inclusive; 30 days before `to` by default.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end, exclusive; now by default.

200.description: The page's unique visitors and conversions

403.description: The caller may not read marketing forms

422.description: No path, or the period ends before it starts or spans over a year

get.description:
How many people the list holds, estimated or exact, and how many can be reached for a purpose,
computed as the caller.

parameters.name: exact
parameters.description: Evaluate the list instead of estimating.

parameters.name: purpose_key
parameters.description: Also count the people reachable for this consent purpose by email.

200.description: The list's size and, for a purpose, how many are reachable

post.summary: Start an email campaign to a list.
post.description:
Renders the design once, fixes the consenting recipients and starts
sending on the bulk stream in the background, at most three marketing
messages per person per week.

422.description: No subject or purpose, a design that does not render, or nobody to email

get.description: Why one person is or is not in the list, condition by condition.

200.description: Which step put the person in or left them out

404.description: No such list, or a person the caller cannot read

post.summary: Import people into a static list from a CSV document.
post.description:
Queues the import; its first column is an email or a record id per row.
Follow it with the import's status route.

404.description: No such list, or the document is not readable

get.description: Rows read, people added and skipped, and whether it finished or failed.

post.description:
Removes exactly the people that import added, within seven days of its
finish.

409.description: Not finished, or finished more than seven days ago

post.summary: Add people to a static list.
post.description:
By hand or from a view selection; only people the caller may read are
added, and people already in the list are skipped.

422.description: A segment list, or more than 1,000 people

get.description: Who was in the list on a past date, as the caller may read them.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: The moment to read the list as of.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

200.description: The people in the list at that time that the caller may read

post.summary: Remove people from a static list.
post.description: Each removal is a membership event; people not in the list are skipped.

422.description: A segment list, or more than 1,000 people

get.description: A few of the list's people the caller may read.

200.description: Up to 20 people of the list the caller may read

post.summary: Estimate an SMS campaign to a list.
post.description:
How many of the list's people can be texted for the purpose, the
message's encoding and segments, and the cost at the configured price.

200.description: Who can be reached and what it costs

422.description: No body or purpose, or the body is too long

x-audit-exempt.note: estimates an SMS campaign; sends and writes nothing

post.summary: Start an SMS campaign to a list.
post.description:
Fixes the consenting recipients and starts sending in the background,
holding each message until the recipient's quiet hours end.

422.description: No body or purpose, or nobody to text

get.description:
How much of a won opportunity each marketing touch earned under one
model, by touch and by campaign; computed nightly.

404.description: No such opportunity, or not readable

post.description:
A score from 0 to 100 (70 passes) and the findings behind it: spam
wording, image-heavy content, links to domains on a blocklist this
deployment checked in the last week, a missing unsubscribe link or text
part, size, and the audience's never-mailed and invalid shares. Each
finding names a guidance key; nothing is sent or stored.

x-audit-exempt.note: scores a message; sends and writes nothing

post.description:
Up to 500 events per batch, 60 batches a minute per caller. Each names
a contact or an anonymous id; events that fail a check come back with
their index and reason, and the rest are kept.

422.description: An empty batch, or more than 500 events

get.description:
The sessions seen in the last five minutes (bots left out), newest
first, each with the page it is on and the known contact or lead.

200.description: Sessions seen in the last five minutes, newest first

get.description:
The page an email's unsubscribe link opens: one button that confirms.
Public; opening it changes nothing (link scanners open links).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token from the email's unsubscribe link

200.description: A page with one unsubscribe button

post.description:
The page's button, or a mail client's one-click request (RFC 8058):
the address stops getting bulk mail. Public; the token is the
credential, and an unknown one answers the same page.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token from the email's unsubscribe link

200.description: Unsubscribed (the same page for any token)

post.description:
Public: the tracking script's batches. Queues them and writes nothing
else; a batch for an unknown or disabled site, from another origin, or
malformed is dropped with the same 204.

requestBody.description: The script's batch, as JSON: {site, visitor, session, events}

204.description: Not taken (the same answer for every reason)

429.description: Too many batches from this visitor or address

get.description:
The site's configuration and the script, cached for a day. Public: a
website loads it with a script tag.

200.description: The tracking script for the site

404.description: No such tracked site (the same answer for every reason)

AlertView.description: One alert raised by the daily evaluation (E6-T10).

guidance_key.description: The screens' translation key for what to do (`deliverabilityAlert.<kind>`).

Attribution.description: An opportunity's credit under one model.

computed_at.description: When it was last computed; `None` when not yet.

BlocklistStatus.description: The latest check of one target on one blocklist.

events.description: All events kept for the contact.

last_seen_at.description: The latest event of any kind.

total_purchases.description: The sum of purchase events' numeric `amount`.

alerts.description: The 100 newest alerts in the window.

bounce_limit.description: The bounce and complaint limits in force, in percent.

sends.description: The 50 largest sends in the window.

DmarcShare.description: DMARC messages for one domain and how many passed (SPF or DKIM aligned).

unauthorised.description: Sources whose every message failed both SPF and DKIM.

stored.description: False when this reporter's report was already stored.

DynamicPreview.description: A preview of a design as one contact or lead sees it.

choices.description: Block id to the chosen variant id (absent: the default).

design.description: The email designer's JSON (E2-T1): blocks, direction, width, colour.

purpose_key.description: The consent purpose the email is sent under.

recipients.description: People who will be emailed, before caps and later withdrawals.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

ExplainStep.description: One step of why a person is in a list or not.

holds.description: Whether the step's list holds the person.

member_after.description: Whether the person is in after this step.

step.description: `base` (the list's own query or members), then each combination.

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

captcha_token.description: The solved challenge, when the deployment asks for one.

fields.description:
The form's fields, consent checkboxes (`consent_<purpose>`), UTM tags
and `page_url`, as the form sent them.

FromListBody.description: Adding a list to a campaign.

list_id.description: The marketing list whose people become members.

purpose.description:
The consent purpose; required for an email, social, advertising or
content campaign.

consent_checked.description: Whether people without consent for the purpose are skipped.

anonymous_id.description: A visitor not yet known as a contact.

kind.description: What happened (1 to 100 characters), such as `page_view` or `purchase`.

LandingStats.description: One landing page's results over a period.

conversion_rate.description: Conversions over unique visitors; absent with no visitors.

LockedField.description:
One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is
`hidden` or `disabled`. No value is ever echoed.

promoted.description: The waiting registration that took the freed seat.

first_check_in.description: False when the person had already been checked in.

reachable.description:
People with active consent for the purpose, an email that is not
suppressed, and no marketing sunset.

ticket_code.description: The ticket code the QR shows.

skipped.description: Ids skipped: already in (or not in) the list, or not readable.

by_status.description: Count per status; a member without one counts under `none`.

person_ids.description: The people (records of the list's target entity), at most 1,000.

PaginatedResponse_DeliverabilityDay.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_IdentityConflict.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

items.description: An identifier claimed by two contacts.

conflict_with.description: The contact it is linked to.

contact_id.description: The contact the identifier was last seen with.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_LiveVisitor.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

contact_ref.description: The known contact or lead, when the visitor is identified.

current_url.description: The page the visitor last viewed.

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PaginatedResponse_String.description: The platform's canonical list envelope (guidelines §12). `total` is the size of the whole set, not of `items`. `page` echoes the page served; every offset list is one-based (D-793): page 1 is the first page. `warnings` is sent only when there is one (Z14-T6).

warnings.description:
Z14-T6: what the caller should know though the list succeeded;
omitted when empty.

PrecheckBody.description: A message to check before sending.

recipients.description:
The audience: how many, how many never mailed before, how many with
an invalid address.

text.description: The plain-text part, if the message has one.

detail.description: What matched (a phrase, a domain), when there is one.

guidance_key.description: The screens' translation key for what to do about it.

PrecheckSeverity.description: How much a finding costs the score.

design.description: The email design (blocks, direction, width, colour).

ProviderDay.description: One provider's totals on one day.

RejectedEvent.description: An event left out, by its place in the batch.

contact_id.description: The contact the identifier is linked to now.

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

SendTotals.description: One send's totals over the window.

expected_cost.description:
`send` only: the cost the sender agreed to; a larger estimate is
refused.

purpose_key.description: The consent purpose the message is sent under.

cost.description:
`total_segments` at `marketing.sms_price_per_segment`; absent when no
price is set.

recipients.description: People with a phone and SMS consent for the purpose.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
